title: How well the fleet does over weeks: experience views in SQL, the decision ladder, escalations, interventions, outcomes, landings per day and idle missions over 24 h, 7 d and 30 d, on the Scorecard's 'How the fleet decides'
prompt:
Read docs/fleet-architecture.md §4 "Experience" and §9 "Not built" (experience views in SQL; ladder health over long periods), docs/design.md §15 (the scorecard's definitions: an intervention under autonomy (a)-(d), a landing and the open-task intervals under throughput, the rounding); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`agent_judgements`, `agent_executions`, `spawn_commands`, the control records in `spawn_events`, the reader's grants); crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs `FLEET_HEALTH` (today's 24 h ladder and human decisions per agent-hour); crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard.rs and scorecard/ (its windows, `--until`, the rounding to 3 decimals) and serve.rs (`/api/scorecard`, `/api/fleet`); web/src/fleetDecisions.ts (`DecisionWindow`, `JudgementFigures`, `LadderFigures`, `decisionsFromHealth`), web/src/components/scorecard/ (`ScorecardView.tsx`, `FleetDecisions.tsx`: the section "How the fleet decides") and web/src/scorecard.ts (`WINDOW_PRESETS`); rsi/scenarios/017.sh (seeding a history straight into the log, which must stay green).

The problem. How the fleet decides is measured only for the last 24 h (the decision ladder and human decisions per agent-hour, in `/api/fleet`'s own query) and the last hour (judgements). Nothing says how the fleet does over a week or a month, nothing counts escalations to the supervisor or how long a mission sat with no task in flight, and no view derives decisions, interventions or outcomes from the log, so every figure is computed again by whoever needs it, each its own way.

Required behaviour. (a) Four views in the schema, readable by the reader (`spawn serve`) and the supervisor, each with an `at_ms` column (when it counts) and one row per item: `spawn_decisions` (`at_ms`, `tier`, `session_id`, `agent_id`, `source`): every judgement (`agent_judgements`, at its time) as tier `rules` when its judge is the rules, else `model`; every command (at its creation) as `dispatcher` (principal `spawn-dispatch`), `supervisor` (`spawn_supervisor`), `human` (`human` or `spawn`, the board's and the CLI's), `liveness` (`spawn-liveness`), any other principal as its own tier; `spawn_interventions` (`at_ms`, `kind`, ...): exactly the scorecard's interventions (design §15 autonomy (a)-(d)), `kind` `command`, `resume`, `owner_task` or `cancel_reassign`, so that their count over a window equals autonomy's `interventions` for that window; `spawn_outcomes` (`at_ms`, `outcome`, `task_id`, `mission_id`, `by`): each task's closing record, `landed` (`task.landed`), `accepted` (`task.reviewed` accepted), `cancelled`, `aborted`, `over_budget`; `spawn_escalations` (`at_ms`, `tag`, `command_id`): each distinct tag of the dispatcher's inputs into the supervisor (`Escalation::tag`), counted once at the first command that carried it. (b) `GET /api/scorecard/fleet?window=24h|7d|30d|90d[&until=<RFC 3339>]` (any other window: 400), the window `[until − window, until)` (`until` defaulting to now), from those views and `agent_judgements`/`agent_executions`, as JSON: `window`, `since_ms`, `until_ms`; `ladder` {`rules`,`model`,`dispatcher`,`supervisor`,`human`,`liveness`} and `ladder_extra` (`[[tier, n]]` for any other tier, by tier); `agent_hours` (the executions' running time clipped to the window; one still running counts to `until`); `human_per_agent_hour` (human decisions over agent hours, null with none); `escalations`; `interventions` {`total`, `by_kind`}; `outcomes` {`landed`,`accepted`,`cancelled`,`aborted`,`over_budget`}; `landed_per_day` (landings as the scorecard's throughput counts them, landed plus accepted, over the window's days); `judgements` {`total`, `by_judge`, `judge_unavailable`, `disagreements`, `model_latency_p50_ms`} as `/api/fleet`'s last hour counts them; `missions`: each mission open in the window (from its `mission.added` to its `mission.closed`, clipped), by id, with `hours` (that span), `idle_hours` (the span less the union of its tasks' open intervals, assignment to close, as throughput's open hours count them) and `idle` (true when `idle_hours` is more than half of `hours`). Ratios and hours to 3 decimals as the scorecard rounds. `/api/fleet`'s 24 h ladder and human decisions per agent-hour read the same views, so home and the scorecard agree. (c) The page: web/src/fleetDecisions.ts exports `decisionsFromApi(answer): DecisionWindow` (it must load with node alone: relative .ts imports, `import type` for types, no packages, erasable TypeScript only), labelling the ladder and the judgements with the window in words (`24 h`, `7 d`, `30 d`, `90 d`) and filling the optional fields `landedPerDay`, `escalations` and `idleHoursByMission` (`{mission, text, hours, idleHours, idle}`); the Scorecard's window toggle (`WINDOW_PRESETS`) picks the window the "How the fleet decides" section reads from `/api/scorecard/fleet`, and the section shows landed per day, escalations, interventions and each mission's idle hours as cards beside the two it has (an idle mission marked idle), not a new page.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/043.sh (read its header: the seeded month and every number worked by hand): a fresh database seeded with control records, judgements, executions and commands over 30 days, every window ending at a fixed `until`. (1) The views exist and, filtered to 24 h, 7 d and 30 d, give the hand-worked counts by tier, kind and outcome, and the escalations. (2) `/api/scorecard/fleet` answers each window with exactly the hand-worked figures (a mission idle 32 h of 48 marked idle), and 400 for `window=2d`. (3) Its interventions and landings equal `spawn scorecard --json`'s autonomy interventions and throughput landings for the same windows. (4) `decisionsFromApi`, under node alone, turns the 7 d answer into the page's DecisionWindow (labels `7 d`, counts, human per agent-hour, landed per day, escalations, idle hours with the idle mark). It fails at (1) on rev-b's df2021c3: there is no view `spawn_decisions`.

What it saves. The owner sees from the page whether the fleet needs a person less this month than last, how often the supervisor is escalated to, how many tasks land a day and which missions sit idle, over the windows the scorecard already offers, without a query of their own; RSI and later objectives read the same views instead of re-deriving decisions, interventions and outcomes.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
